subject.title: fix(agents): avoid synthetic overflow in tool-heavy sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public session-SDK `contextOverflowRecoveryOwner` mode, or must this remain an embedded-runner-only coordination detail?
rationale: The patch currently adds a durable API choice while the only demonstrated consumer is internal; selecting a permanent external recovery contract requires owner intent rather than a mechanical review decision.

options.title: Keep it internal
options.body: Remove the exported option and route the embedded runner through a private session-construction seam so public callers retain canonical session-owned recovery.

options.title: Adopt a public API
options.body: Retain the option only with explicit ownership, documented caller obligations, compatibility tests, and a clear reason external SDK clients need it.

recommendation.title: Keep it internal
recommendation.body: Remove the exported option and route the embedded runner through a private session-construction seam so public callers retain canonical session-owned recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence adjacent agent-runtime owner from recent subsystem refactor history.
